statement: Let R⊆E×E′ be a relation, Γ=R its graph (no duplicate edges), f,f′ its projections, and u(S)={y:∃x∈S,(x,y)∈R}. The following are equivalent: u preserves disjointness; u preserves binary intersections; u preserves every nonempty intersection; u preserves S\T for all S,T; it does so for T⊆S; f′ is injective. All joins, including the empty join, are already preserved. The graph hypothesis matters: an arbitrary span with repeated edges need not satisfy the projection characterization.
